hint.importance: How far this subject's effects or fame reach. Helps judge who in the world would know about it.
hint.subjectType: What kind of thing this is: an idea, something that happened, a tale, an unsolved question, a strange occurrence?
hint.associatedCharacters: Characters involved in, affected by or known for this subject.
hint.generic.associatedCultures: Cultures that created, remember or are shaped by this subject.
hint.geography.associatedCultures: Cultures that live there, hold it sacred or come from it.
hint.technology.associatedCultures: Cultures known for using or inventing it.
hint.species.associatedCultures: Cultures this species is part of.
hint.generic.associatedLocations: Places where it happened, is found or is remembered.
hint.associatedOrganizations: Organizations that caused, guard, study or exploit this subject.
hint.generic.associatedReligions: Faiths that revere, fear or explain this subject.
hint.tradition.associatedReligions: Faiths that bless, lead or condemn it.
hint.language.associatedReligions: Faiths that use it in worship or scripture.
hint.consequences: What changed because of it. Consequences are what make a subject matter to the present day.
hint.generic.dateOfOrigin: When it began or first appeared, in your world's calendar.
hint.dateOfResolution: When it ended or was resolved, if it has been.
hint.origin: How or where it started. The seed of the story.
hint.precedingSubject: The event, legend or concept that came right before this one or led to it.
hint.generic.status: Where it stands today: still happening, long past, coming back, argued over, lost to memory?
hint.character.status: Are they alive, dead, missing? Drives the Status grouping of the Characters folder.
hint.playerCharacter.status: Are they alive, dead, missing? Drives the Status grouping of the Characters folder.
hint.organization.status: Is it thriving, fading, gone, or hiding? Tells the party whether it can still help or hurt them.
hint.settlement.status: Is it on the rise, holding steady, fading, or in ruins?
hint.military.status: Whether it still exists and fights.
hint.title.status: Is the title held, empty, contested or gone?
hint.tradition.status: How alive the tradition is today.
hint.item.status: What state the item is in today.
hint.language.status: How alive the language is today.
hint.alignment: Their moral and ethical compass: do they follow order or freedom, good or evil? A quick guide for playing them consistently.
hint.gender: How society and culture classify this character, and how they see themselves. Different cultures may understand gender in very different ways.
hint.house: The noble or great house this character belongs to by birth, marriage or adoption. Drives succession and the House grouping.
hint.lastSeen: Where this character was last spotted. Handy for tracking where the party can find them next.
hint.nickname: What friends, rivals or the common folk call them. A good nickname tells a story on its own.
hint.organizations: Guilds, orders, councils or clans this character is a member of. Shows where their loyalties and resources come from.
hint.sex: The character's biological sex, as their species understands it. Useful for lineage, heirs and how others first perceive them.
hint.ethnicity: The people or bloodline they descend from. Shapes their looks, customs and how strangers treat them.
hint.eyes: Eye color, size, shape? Anything striking, like a scar or a glow?
hint.hair: Color, length, style? Braided, shaved, greying at the temples?
hint.height: How tall are they? A number, or a comparison like "towers over most men".
hint.species: Human, elf, dwarf…? Links to the Species article that describes their kind.
hint.weight: How heavy are they? Slight, stocky, a number — whatever reads best at the table.
hint.age: How old are they? Years, or a feel like "young adult" or "ancient" if it's unknown.
hint.dateOfBirth: When they were born, in your world's calendar. Anchors them on the timeline.
hint.dateOfDeath: When they died, if they have. Leave empty for the living.
hint.birthplace: The settlement, territory or building where they were born. Roots often explain loyalties and accents.
hint.culture: The cultures they were raised in or adopted. Shapes their customs, values and worldview.
hint.education: Where and how they learned: a temple school, a master's workshop, the streets?
hint.formerOccupations: Jobs they held before. Old skills and old contacts tend to resurface.
hint.character.languages: The languages they speak, read or write. Decides who they can talk to — and eavesdrop on.
hint.playerCharacter.languages: The languages they speak, read or write. Decides who they can talk to — and eavesdrop on.
hint.settlement.languages: The languages spoken in its streets.
hint.occupation: What they do for a living right now.
hint.residence: Where they live now: a specific building or a settlement. Tells the party where to knock.
hint.socialBackground: The background they come from, as in the player's handbook. A shortcut to their skills and past.
hint.ambitions: What they want most. Ambitions are what push a character into the story.
hint.fears: What they dread or avoid. Fears make great pressure points in a scene.
hint.flaws: A vice, weakness or blind spot others could exploit.
hint.ideals: The principles they believe in and would fight for.
hint.character.reputation: What people say about them, true or not. It arrives before they do.
hint.playerCharacter.reputation: What people say about them, true or not. It arrives before they do.
hint.military.reputation: How friends and foes see it.
hint.character.allies: Characters and organizations they can count on when things go wrong.
hint.playerCharacter.allies: Characters and organizations they can count on when things go wrong.
hint.territory.allies: Realms, organizations and characters it can count on when war comes.
hint.children: Their sons and daughters, by blood or adoption.
hint.deities: The gods, patrons or higher powers they worship or serve.
hint.character.enemies: Characters and organizations that want them gone. Rivalries drive conflict.
hint.playerCharacter.enemies: Characters, fellow players' characters and organizations that want them gone. Rivalries drive conflict.
hint.territory.enemies: Realms, organizations and characters that want it weakened or gone.
hint.mentors: Who taught them what they know.
hint.religion: The faiths they follow or were raised in.
hint.siblings: Their brothers and sisters — allies, rivals or both.
hint.titles: Titles they hold or have held, like knighthoods or offices.
hint.controllingPlayer: The real person at the table who plays this character. Handy when a player misses a session or hands the character over.
hint.classSubclass: Their class and subclass, e.g. "Paladin / Oath of Vengeance". Multiclassed? List each one.
hint.levelMilestone: Their level, or the last milestone they reached. Keeps encounters balanced and rewards on track.
hint.arcStatus: Where their personal story stands right now. Tells you whether it's time to build tension or pay it off.
hint.personalQuest: What is their overarching ultimate goal? The thread you can weave the campaign's big moments around.
hint.shortTermMotivations: What is driving them in the current story arc? Hooks for the next few sessions.
hint.family: Relatives in the world: people the villain can threaten and the hero will ride out to save.
hint.friends: NPCs and fellow party members they trust. Friends are allies in a pinch and heartbreak when they turn.
hint.partyRole: The part they usually play in the group. Shows gaps in the party and who takes the lead in a scene.
hint.oathsPacts: Vows, pacts and bargains they're bound by, and with whom. A broken oath is a story waiting to happen.
hint.bounties: Active prices on their head or legal troubles they are fleeing. The past catching up with them.
hint.titlesEarned: Nicknames, formal knighthoods or arena champion titles won in-game. Proof of what they've done.
hint.color: The house's color. Its members wear it on family trees and relationship webs, so a glance tells the dynasties apart.
hint.foundedOn: When the organization was founded, in your world's calendar.
hint.organization.founders: The characters or organizations that created it. Founders often shape its creed for centuries.
hint.religion.founders: Prophets or saints who founded it.
hint.motto: Its words, creed or battle cry. A motto sums up what it stands for.
hint.organizationType: What kind of organization this is. Also groups it in the Organizations folder.
hint.admissionRequirements: What it takes to join: a bloodline, a fee, a deed, an oath?
hint.organization.leaders: The characters who run it today.
hint.settlement.leaders: Mayors, lords, elders — whoever is in charge.
hint.membershipSize: How many members it has — a number, or a feel like "a handful" or "thousands".
hint.notableMembers: Members worth knowing about, even if they don't lead.
hint.ranks: The titles that make up its internal hierarchy.
hint.organization.recruitmentMethod: How new members come in. Pick every way that applies.
hint.military.recruitmentMethod: How it fills its ranks. Pick every way that applies.
hint.alliedOrganizations: Organizations it cooperates with or can call on.
hint.goals: What it is trying to achieve. Goals are what put it at odds with others.
hint.parentOrganization: The larger organization this one belongs to or answers to.
hint.rivalOrganizations: Organizations competing with it or working against it.
hint.subordinateOrganizations: Branches, chapters or vassal groups under its control.
hint.assets: Buildings and items it owns or guards.
hint.organization.fundingSources: Where its money comes from: dues, trade, tithes, crime, patrons?
hint.military.fundingSources: Who pays for it: the crown, taxes, plunder, a patron?
hint.headquarters: The building or settlement it operates from.
hint.operatingTerritories: Territories where it is active or holds influence.
hint.publicInfluence: How much sway it has over ordinary people and rulers.
hint.territory.parentTerritory: The larger territory this one belongs to. Only types the hierarchy profile allows are offered; leave it out for a root realm.
hint.settlement.parentTerritory: The territory this settlement belongs to.
hint.area: How large the territory is — a figure, or a feel like "three days' ride across".
hint.borders: The territories and natural features along its borders. Neighbors make allies and wars.
hint.containedSettlements: The cities, towns and villages inside it.
hint.geographicFeatures: Mountains, rivers, forests and other landmarks within it.
hint.territory.seasonProfile: Which season schedule (from Calendars) this territory follows, so its current season shows here. Leave it out when seasons don't matter.
hint.geography.seasonProfile: Which season schedule (from Calendars) this place follows, so its current season shows here. The region picks it; Calendars never assigns one.
hint.territory.strategicLocations: Forts, passes, ports or crossings that whoever holds them controls the land.
hint.conflict.strategicLocations: Places both sides fight to hold.
hint.capital: The settlement it is ruled from.
hint.claimants: Those who say the land is rightfully theirs, ruling or not. A rival claim is a war waiting to happen.
hint.governingBody: The council, house or institution that governs it.
hint.governmentForm: How power is organized: one ruler, the people, a few families, the faith?
hint.rulingTitles: The titles its rulers hold, like King or High Chancellor.
hint.territory.establishedOn: When the territory was founded or first recognized.
hint.formerRulers: Characters or organizations that once ruled it. Old claims rarely die quietly.
hint.territory.historicalEvents: Wars, treaties, disasters and other events that shaped it.
hint.geography.historicalEvents: Battles, disasters and other events that happened there.
hint.politicalStatus: Does it answer to no one, serve an overlord, or has it been taken or dissolved?
hint.cultures: The cultures of the people living there.
hint.laws: Laws in force across the territory.
hint.territory.population: How many people live there — a number, or a feel like "sparse" or "teeming".
hint.settlement.population: How many people live there — a number, or a feel like "a few dozen".
hint.territory.speciesPresent: The peoples and creatures that live there in numbers.
hint.settlement.speciesPresent: The peoples that live there in numbers.
hint.culture.speciesPresent: The species that share this culture.
hint.fauna: Animals living here. What hunters bring back, and what the party hears at night.
hint.flora: Plants and fungi growing here. The herbs a healer forages for, the poison a rogue might find.
hint.monsters: Monsters known to roam or lair here. The reason locals stay home after dark.
hint.governingOrganization: The council, guild or house that runs the settlement.
hint.localLaws: Laws that apply here in particular. Strangers tend to break these first.
hint.settlementType: How big and permanent it is, from a lone farm to a sprawling metropolis.
hint.defenses: Walls, watch, garrison, wards? How well can it hold off a threat?
hint.notableBuildings: Buildings worth a visit: temples, taverns, keeps, markets.
hint.publicServices: What the settlement provides: roads, healers, schools, sewers, a postal service?
hint.waterSupply: The rivers, lakes, wells or aqueducts it drinks from. Cut the water and the town falls.
hint.notableResidents: Characters who live there and are worth knowing.
hint.exports: What it sells to the world.
hint.imports: What it has to buy from elsewhere. Dependencies make leverage.
hint.industries: What people there do for work: fishing, mining, weaving, smuggling?
hint.tradePartners: Settlements and organizations it trades with regularly.
hint.wealthLevel: How well-off the settlement is overall. Sets prices, crime and what's for sale.
hint.architects: The characters or organizations that designed or built it.
hint.architecturalStyle: What it looks like: soaring gothic spires, squat dwarven stone, elven living wood?
hint.builtOn: When it was built, in your world's calendar.
hint.constructionMaterials: What it's made of. Timber burns, stone endures, and some materials are rarer than gold.
hint.sizeAndLayout: How big it is and how it's arranged: floors, wings, cellars, secret passages?
hint.structuralCondition: What shape it's in today, from pristine to a pile of rubble.
hint.buildingType: What kind of building this is.
hint.currentUse: What it's used for now — which may not be what it was built for.
hint.formerUse: What it used to be. Old purposes leave old secrets.
hint.publicAccess: Who can walk in. Tells the party whether they need a key, a password or a plan.
hint.servicesOffered: What visitors can get here: rooms, healing, training, goods, answers?
hint.associatedGeography: The natural features it stands on, beside or within.
hint.connectedBuildings: Buildings linked to this one by bridges, tunnels or shared walls.
hint.parentBuilding: The larger building or complex this one is part of.
hint.caretaker: Who looks after it day to day, if not the owner.
hint.occupants: Who lives or works there now.
hint.building.previousOwners: Who owned it before. Some may want it back.
hint.item.previousOwners: Who held it before. Some may want it back.
hint.climate: The usual weather over the year. Decides what travelers need to pack.
hint.commonWildlife: The animals and monsters most often seen there.
hint.environmentalHazards: What can kill the unwary: quicksand, avalanches, poison mists, wild magic?
hint.notableSpecies: Species that live there or are known from there.
hint.primaryBiome: The main kind of landscape and ecosystem found there.
hint.seasonalChanges: How it changes through the year: floods, frozen rivers, migrations?
hint.elevationOrDepth: How high it rises or how deep it goes.
hint.featureType: What kind of geographic feature this is.
hint.naturalResources: Timber, ore, game, herbs, gems? Resources are what people fight over.
hint.sizeOrExtent: How large it is, or how far it stretches.
hint.unusualProperties: Anything strange about it: floating rocks, time slipping, whispering trees?
hint.legends: Tales told about the place, true or not.
hint.religiousSignificance: Faiths that consider it holy, cursed or important.
hint.ruinsAndStructures: Buildings and ruins found there. Perfect dungeon material.
hint.adjacentFeatures: Natural features that border this one.
hint.containedFeatures: Smaller features inside this one, like peaks in a range or islands in a sea.
hint.nearbySettlements: Settlements within reach. Where travelers can rest or resupply.
hint.overlappingTerritories: Territories it lies in or crosses.
hint.parentGeographicFeature: The larger feature this one is part of.
hint.commandStructure: How orders flow: a single general, a council of captains, a chain of lords?
hint.officerPositions: The ranks and offices of its officers.
hint.parentFormation: The larger force this one belongs to.
hint.successionOfCommand: Who takes over if the commander falls. Armies break when nobody knows.
hint.eliteUnits: Its best units, the ones sent where it matters.
hint.recruitmentRequirements: What it takes to join: age, strength, birth, an oath?
hint.speciesRepresented: The species serving in its ranks.
hint.training: How its soldiers are trained, and how long it takes.
hint.unitSpecialization: What its troops are trained to do. Pick every specialty that applies.
hint.commonArmors: The armor its soldiers usually wear.
hint.commonWeapons: The weapons its soldiers usually carry.
hint.magicalCapabilities: The schools of magic it can bring to a battle.
hint.mountsAndWarBeasts: Horses, griffons, war elephants — the creatures it rides or unleashes.
hint.siegeEquipment: Rams, trebuchets, siege towers and stranger engines.
hint.signatureEquipments: Gear it's known for — the thing enemies recognize from afar.
hint.vehiclesAndVessels: Wagons, warships, airships and whatever else carries it to war.
hint.allegiance: Who it serves. Loyalty can be bought, sworn or inherited.
hint.formationType: What kind of force this is.
hint.mottoOrBattleCry: What its soldiers shout as they charge.
hint.serviceType: How it serves: always under arms, called up when needed, or for hire?
hint.medicalSupport: Who tends its wounded: surgeons, clerics, nobody?
hint.payAndCompensation: What its soldiers earn. Unpaid armies rarely stay loyal.
hint.supplySources: Where its food, arms and horses come from.
hint.transportAndSupplyMethods: How supplies reach the front: wagon trains, ships, portals, foraging?
hint.combatDoctrine: How it prefers to fight: shield walls, ambushes, overwhelming magic?
hint.currentObjectives: What it's trying to achieve right now.
hint.militaryAllies: Forces and organizations that fight alongside it.
hint.militaryEnemies: Forces and organizations it fights against.
hint.readiness: How ready it is to fight at a moment's notice.
hint.competingClaims: What each side claims is rightfully theirs.
hint.immediateTrigger: The spark that set it off.
hint.objectivesOfEachSide: What each side wants to walk away with.
hint.underlyingTensions: Cultures, faiths, laws or organizations at the heart of the tension.
hint.violatedAgreements: Treaties or laws that were broken.
hint.escalation: How it grew from its first spark.
hint.interventions: Outside powers that stepped in, and how.
hint.negotiations: Attempts to talk it out, and how they went.
hint.turningPoints: The moments that changed its direction.
hint.conflictType: What kind of conflict this is. Pick every kind that applies.
hint.parentConflict: The larger conflict this one is part of.
hint.publicAwareness: How much the world knows about it.
hint.attackersAllies: Allies of the attackers who joined the war.
hint.defendersAllies: Allies of the defenders who joined the war.
hint.externalSupporters: Outsiders backing a side with gold, arms or words.
hint.balanceOfPower: Which side holds the advantage, and why.
hint.fundingAndSupplies: How each side pays for and feeds its fight.
hint.intelligenceAndEspionage: Spies, scouts and secrets in play.
hint.unconventionalMethods: Tricks, sabotage or tactics nobody expected.
hint.casualtiesAndLosses: What it cost in lives and property.
hint.displacedPopulations: Who was driven from their homes.
hint.economicEffects: What it did to trade, prices and fortunes.
hint.outcome: How it ended — or where it stands.
hint.resolutionMethod: How it came to an end.
hint.settlementAgreements: Treaties and accords that ended it.
hint.unresolvedIssues: What was left unsettled — the seeds of the next conflict.
hint.endedOn: When it ended, if it has.
hint.precedingConflicts: Conflicts that led to this one.
hint.conflictingAccounts: Documents that tell the story differently.
hint.historicalEvidence: What's left that proves it happened.
hint.unansweredQuestions: Mysteries it left behind — great hooks for a campaign.
hint.accessibility: Who is allowed to know how it works.
hint.species.distribution: How widespread they are across the world.
hint.legalRestrictions: Laws that limit or ban it.
hint.language.usingOrganizations: Guilds, orders or cabals that use it.
hint.civilianUses: What ordinary people use it for.
hint.implementedIn: Items and buildings that use it.
hint.militaryUses: How armies put it to use.
hint.socialImpact: How it changed daily life, work or power.
hint.competingTechnologies: Rival approaches to the same problem.
hint.developmentStatus: How far along it is, from an idea on paper to a forgotten relic.
hint.replacedBy: Newer technologies that made it obsolete.
hint.fieldOfApplication: The areas it's used in. Pick every field that applies.
hint.technologyType: What kind of technology this is.
hint.operatingPrinciples: How it works, in a sentence or two.
hint.operatingRequirements: What it needs to run: fuel, crew, calm weather, a full moon?
hint.powerSource: What drives it. Pick every source that applies.
hint.requiredExpertise: The skills needed to operate it.
hint.requiredMagic: Spells or magic it depends on.
hint.requiredTechnologies: Other technologies it can't work without.
hint.technicalDocumentation: Manuals, schematics and notes describing it.
hint.byproducts: What it leaves behind: smoke, slag, waste, residue?
hint.productionFacilities: Workshops and foundries where it's made.
hint.productionTime: How long it takes to make one.
hint.requiredTools: The tools needed to build it.
hint.environmentalEffects: What it does to the land, water and air around it.
hint.failureModes: How it breaks — and what happens when it does.
hint.maintenanceRequirements: The upkeep it needs to keep working.
hint.safetyHazards: The dangers to whoever uses it.
hint.vulnerabilities: How an enemy could sabotage or exploit it.
hint.appointingAuthority: Who grants this title. Whoever grants it can usually take it away.
hint.duties: What the holder is expected to do.
hint.title.jurisdiction: The lands, settlements or organizations where the title's authority applies.
hint.law.jurisdiction: The lands, settlements or organizations where the law holds.
hint.legalBasis: The laws or documents that create and define the title.
hint.powers: What the holder can command, decide or forbid.
hint.privileges: What the holder enjoys: income, immunity, land, precedence at court?
hint.currentHolders: The characters holding the title today.
hint.formerHolders: Characters who held it before. A lineage of names carries weight.
hint.seatOfOffice: Where the holder rules or works from.
hint.formOfAddress: How the holder is addressed: Your Grace, My Lord, Honored One?
hint.insigniaOrRegalia: The crowns, seals, rings or robes that mark the holder.
hint.rank: Where the title sits in its hierarchy.
hint.superiorTitle: The title this one answers to.
hint.titleType: What kind of title this is. Pick every kind that applies.
hint.eligibilityRequirements: Who may hold it: bloodline, faith, age, a test?
hint.removalConditions: How a holder can lose the title.
hint.successionMethod: How the next holder is chosen.
hint.successionRules: The details of succession — and the loopholes heirs fight over.
hint.termLength: How long a holder keeps it: for life, seven years, until the next moon?
hint.enactedBy: Who made this law. Whoever made it can usually unmake it.
hint.enactedOn: When the law was passed or proclaimed, in your world's calendar.
hint.legalTradition: The cultures or faiths whose customs this law grows out of.
hint.sourceDocument: The charter, codex or decree where the law is written down.
hint.appealProcess: How a verdict can be challenged, and before whom — if at all.
hint.enforcementConsistency: How reliably it's actually enforced. A law on paper and a law in the streets are different things.
hint.enforcingOrganizations: The watch, courts, inquisitors or guilds that uphold it.
hint.judicialAuthority: Who judges those accused of breaking it.
hint.penalties: What happens to those who break it: fines, exile, the gallows?
hint.affectedGroups: Who the law applies to: everyone, nobles, foreigners, spellcasters?
hint.exceptions: Who or what is exempt. Loopholes are where the stories are.
hint.lawType: What areas of life the law covers. Pick every kind that applies.
hint.requirementsOrProhibitions: What the law demands or forbids, in plain words.
hint.amendedBy: Later laws that changed this one.
hint.effectiveFrom: When the law took effect, if not when it was enacted.
hint.expiresOn: When the law lapses, if it has an end date.
hint.firstRecordedOn: The earliest known record of the tradition.
hint.originStory: How people say it began — the true story may differ.
hint.regionalVariations: How it differs from place to place. Doing it the "wrong" way can start a fight.
hint.eligibility: Who may take part: everyone, adults, the initiated, one family?
hint.organizers: The characters or organizations that run it.
hint.practicedIn: Territories and settlements where it's observed.
hint.requiredRoles: Titles someone must hold for the tradition to take place, like a high priest or a herald.
hint.activities: What people actually do: feast, dance, fast, duel, burn effigies?
hint.tradition.duration: How long it lasts: an hour, a night, a week?
hint.requiredItems: Objects the tradition can't happen without.
hint.timingOrTrigger: When it happens, or what sets it off: a full moon, a birth, a first kill?
hint.traditionType: What kind of tradition this is. Pick every kind that applies.
hint.meaning: What the tradition means to those who keep it.
hint.symbolism: The colors, objects and gestures and what they stand for.
hint.tradition.taboos: What must never be done during it. A gift for your plot.
hint.culture.taboos: What is never done or said. Outsiders break these first.
hint.attitudesTowardMagic: Is magic revered, feared, regulated or ordinary? Spellcasters will want to know.
hint.coreValues: What this people prizes most: honor, family, knowledge, freedom?
hint.hospitalityCustoms: How guests are welcomed, and what a guest owes in return.
hint.viewsOnDeath: How they understand death, and how they treat their dead.
hint.architecture: What their buildings look like, and why.
hint.artAndMusic: Their crafts, songs, instruments and favorite subjects.
hint.clothing: How they dress, and what clothing says about rank or role.
hint.cuisine: What they eat and drink, and what's served on special days.
hint.namingCustoms: How names are chosen and built. Handy for naming NPCs on the fly.
hint.traditions: The festivals, rites and customs it keeps.
hint.regionsPracticed: Territories and settlements where this culture lives today.
hint.relatedCultures: Cultures sharing its roots or strongly shaped by it.
hint.familyStructures: How families and households are organized, and who holds authority in them.
hint.leadershipCustoms: How leaders are chosen and what is expected of them.
hint.socialClasses: The layers of society, and how hard it is to move between them.
hint.viewsOnOutsiders: How strangers are treated — useful for the party's first welcome.
hint.bodyStructure: How the body is built: limbs, wings, tails, shells?
hint.creatureType: Its creature type, as in the Monster Manual. Decides which spells and features affect it.
hint.distinguishingFeatures: What makes one recognizable at a glance.
hint.movement: How they get around: walk, fly, swim, burrow, slither?
hint.senses: How they perceive the world: darkvision, tremorsense, keen smell?
hint.species.typicalHeight: How tall an average adult stands.
hint.fauna.typicalHeight: How tall (or long) a grown adult is.
hint.typicalSize: Their size categories. Pick every size individuals commonly reach.
hint.species.typicalWeight: How much an average adult weighs.
hint.fauna.typicalWeight: How much a grown adult weighs. Handy when someone tries to carry one.
hint.monster.typicalWeight: How much it weighs. Matters for bridges, boats and trapdoors.
hint.adaptations: How they've adapted to where they live.
hint.species.diet: What they eat — and whether the party is on the menu.
hint.fauna.diet: What it eats, and how it gets it: grazing, hunting, scavenging?
hint.environmentalVulnerabilities: Conditions they can't endure: sunlight, cold, dry air?
hint.preferredHabitat: The kind of place they thrive in.
hint.classification: How scholars classify them: humanoid, beast, fey, aberration?
hint.originAccount: How they came to be, according to legend or scholars.
hint.fauna.relatedSpecies: Close relatives: wild cousins, domestic breeds, monstrous offshoots.
hint.flora.relatedSpecies: Close relatives: wild cousins, cultivated varieties, ancestral forms.
hint.subspeciesOrLineages: Distinct branches of this species, like high elves and wood elves.
hint.lifeStages: The stages of their life: larva, youngling, elder?
hint.species.reproduction: How they reproduce and raise their young.
hint.fauna.reproduction: How it breeds and raises its young: eggs, litters, nests, a mating season?
hint.innateAbilities: Powers they're born with: breath weapons, resistances, spells?
hint.populationTrend: Whether their numbers are growing or shrinking.
hint.anatomyAndAppearance: What it looks like: body shape, limbs, fur, scales or feathers? Anything a hunter would recognize at a glance.
hint.coloration: Its colors and markings. Does it blend in, warn off, or change with the seasons?
hint.fauna.size: Its size category. Decides the space it takes and what it can carry or swallow.
hint.monster.size: Its size category. Decides the space it takes and what it can grapple or swallow.
hint.activityCycle: When it's awake and about. Decides whether the night watch hears it.
hint.seasonalBehavior: What changes with the seasons: migration, hibernation, mating displays, molting?
hint.socialStructure: Solitary, pairs, herds, packs or colonies? How big a group the party runs into.
hint.temperament: How it reacts to people: skittish, curious, territorial, aggressive?
hint.animalGroup: The broad kind of animal it is.
hint.existenceStatus: Does it still exist? A creature everyone thinks extinct makes a fine rumor to chase.
hint.fauna.abundance: How easy it is to come across this animal. Sets how often it shows up in encounters and markets.
hint.flora.abundance: How easy it is to come across this plant. Sets how often it shows up in encounters and markets.
hint.monster.abundance: How easy it is to come across this creature. Sets how often it shows up in encounters and markets.
hint.fauna.biomes: The kinds of landscape where this animal lives. Pick every one it's found in.
hint.flora.biomes: The kinds of landscape where this plant lives. Pick every one it's found in.
hint.monster.biomes: The kinds of landscape where this creature lives. Pick every one it's found in.
hint.climates: The climates it can live in. Helps decide what the party meets on the road.
hint.distributionNotes: How far it ranges and where it's thickest: seasonal migrations, isolated pockets, a single valley?
hint.foundIn: Places where it lives: territories, geographic regions, even a single building. They list it back under their own Fauna, Flora or Monsters.
hint.habitatDescription: Where exactly it makes its home: treetops, riverbanks, old ruins? Tells the party where to look.
hint.fauna.ecologicalRole: What it does for its surroundings: grazer, pollinator, apex predator, scavenger?
hint.flora.ecologicalRole: What it does for its surroundings: shelter, food, holding the soil, choking out rivals?
hint.predators: What hunts it. Where there's prey, there may be something bigger nearby.
hint.preyAndFoodSources: The animals and plants it lives on.
hint.characterSheet: A web address for its stat block (D&D Beyond, a homebrew page, a shared sheet), to open it at the table.
hint.lifespan: How long it usually lives, in the wild and in captivity.
hint.fauna.culturalSignificance: What it means to people: a sacred animal, a heraldic beast, an omen, a children's tale?
hint.flora.culturalSignificance: What it means to people: a sacred tree, a wedding flower, a plant no one dares to cut?
hint.magic.culturalSignificance: What it means to the people who use it.
hint.language.culturalSignificance: What the language means to its speakers.
hint.domestication: Whether it can be tamed, bred, ridden or trained, and who does it.
hint.fauna.productsAndUses: What people take from it: meat, hide, milk, feathers, venom, labor? Worth coin at the market.
hint.flora.productsAndUses: What people make from it: food, timber, cloth, dye, perfume, fuel? Worth coin at the market.
hint.risksToPeople: How it can hurt people: bites, disease, crop raids, stampedes?
hint.identifyingFeatures: How to tell it apart: leaves, bark, flowers, scent? What a Nature check would pick up on.
hint.seasonalAppearance: How it looks through the year: blossoms, fruit, bare branches, dormant bulbs?
hint.sizeAndGrowthShape: How big it gets and how it grows: towering, sprawling, climbing, underground?
hint.plantOrFungusGroup: The kinds of plant or fungus it is. Pick more than one for in-betweens, like a vine that grows into a tree.
hint.type: Whether it's an ordinary plant or carries magic. Magical ones are what herbalists and alchemists hunt for.
hint.cultivation: Whether and how people grow it: fields, gardens, greenhouses, secret groves?
hint.harvestingAndStorage: When and how the useful parts are gathered, prepared and kept. A harvest at midnight makes a good errand.
hint.associatedOrganisms: What lives with it: pollinators, grazers, parasites, partners, or the creature that guards it.
hint.growingConditions: What it needs to grow: soil, water, sunlight, altitude, or something stranger like moonlight or graves.
hint.growthAndLifespan: How fast it grows, when it matures and how long it lives.
hint.reproductionAndSpread: How it spreads: seeds, spores, runners, cuttings, or something supernatural?
hint.seasonalCycle: When it flowers, fruits, releases spores or goes dormant, in your world's calendar.
hint.edibility: Which parts can be eaten, and how they must be prepared. Useful when rations run out.
hint.hazards: How it can hurt people: poison, burning sap, thorns, choking spores?
hint.medicinalAndAlchemicalProperties: The remedies, potions and reagents made from it, and what they do.
hint.flora.supernaturalProperties: Its magic, and what sets it off: glowing at night, whispering, blooming only near the dead?
hint.language.supernaturalProperties: Anything uncanny about it: words that burn, names with power?
hint.distinctiveFeatures: What the party sees first: silhouette, texture, colors, the detail survivors always mention.
hint.variationsAndForms: Regional variants, transformations or disguises. The form it takes when no one's looking?
hint.communication: How it communicates: speech, mimicry, telepathy, signs? Can the party talk it down?
hint.feedingAndNeeds: What it feeds on or needs: flesh, heat, memories, dreams, magic? A need is a weakness to exploit.
hint.intelligenceAndMotivations: How clever it is and what it wants. Decides whether it's a beast to fight or a foe to outwit.
hint.socialBehavior: Alone, in packs or in colonies? Who leads, and how it treats its own kind.
hint.territorialBehavior: How it picks, marks and defends its lair. The warning signs the party finds before it finds them.
hint.entryScope: Whether this page is a whole kind of monster, one variant of it, or one particular creature.
hint.relatedCreatures: Its species, variants, relatives or known individuals.
hint.monster.associatedEvents: When it made history: attacks, disasters, battles, its first sighting.
hint.item.associatedEvents: Events it played a part in.
hint.beliefsAndLegends: The tales, songs and writings about it. Half of them are wrong, which half is up to you.
hint.lifespanAndDevelopment: How it ages and grows: metamorphosis, molting, or no aging at all?
hint.reproductionOrCreation: Where new ones come from: eggs, spawning, curses, a mad wizard's lab?
hint.affiliations: Who it's tied to: its creator, master, a cult that worships it, a deity, allies.
hint.afterlifeBeliefs: What the faithful believe happens after death.
hint.centralTeachings: The core of what the faith teaches.
hint.creationAccount: How the faith says the world began.
hint.deitiesOrSacredBeings: The gods, saints, spirits or powers the faith worships.
hint.religiousModel: The shape of the faith: one god, many, spirits in all things, the ancestors?
hint.branchesAndSects: Offshoots and rival interpretations of the faith.
hint.religiousOrders: Monastic, militant or scholarly orders serving the faith.
hint.seatOfAuthority: The temple or holy city the faith is governed from.
hint.conversionRequirements: What it takes to join the faith — if outsiders can join at all.
hint.dailyPractices: Prayers, offerings or habits the faithful keep every day.
hint.funeraryPractices: How the faith treats its dead.
hint.holyDays: Festivals and sacred days of the faith.
hint.pilgrimages: Journeys the faithful are called to make.
hint.rituals: The rites and ceremonies of the faith.
hint.sacredSymbols: The signs and emblems of the faith.
hint.item.articleScope: Is this article about one specific object, a kind of item, a set, a material or something used up?
hint.magic.articleScope: Is this article about a single spell, a ritual, a school, or a whole system of magic?
hint.itemType: What kind of item this is.
hint.rarity: How hard it is to find. Sets its price and who would kill for it.
hint.item.currentLocation: Where it is right now, if nobody is carrying it.
hint.legalOwner: Who it rightfully belongs to — not always who has it.
hint.activationMethod: How its power is used: a command word, a drop of blood, attunement?
hint.appearance: What it looks like, feels like, sounds like.
hint.dimensionsAndWeight: How big and heavy it is.
hint.limitations: Charges, cooldowns or conditions that limit it.
hint.magicalEffects: What it can do beyond the mundane.
hint.mundaneUses: What it's good for without any magic.
hint.item.sideEffects: The price of using it: curses, fatigue, whispers at night?
hint.magic.sideEffects: Unwanted effects on the caster or the world around.
hint.value: What it's worth, in coin or otherwise.
hint.requiredComponents: Items needed to craft it — a good quest hook.
hint.castingTime: How long it takes to cast: an action, a minute, a night of chanting?
hint.components: What casting it requires. Pick every component that applies.
hint.focusItems: Wands, holy symbols or other foci it's channeled through.
hint.materialComponents: The materials used in casting it.
hint.materialRequirements: Costly or consumed materials, and how much of them.
hint.requiredConditions: Conditions that must be met: a place, a time, a phase of the moon?
hint.ritualProcedure: The steps of the ritual, in order.
hint.observableSigns: What onlookers see, hear or smell when it's cast.
hint.secondaryEffects: Lesser effects that come with it.
hint.targetRequirements: What a target must be for it to work.
hint.targets: Who or what it can affect.
hint.dateOfDiscovery: When it was first discovered or created.
hint.magic.learningRequirements: What it takes to learn it: study, a pact, a bloodline?
hint.language.learningRequirements: What it takes to learn it: a teacher, a pact, years of study?
hint.teachingOrganizations: Academies, orders or covens that teach it.
hint.teachingTexts: Spellbooks, grimoires and scrolls that record it.
hint.concentration: Whether the caster must keep focus to sustain it.
hint.costsAndSacrifices: What the caster gives up to cast it.
hint.countersAndDefenses: How it can be blocked, dispelled or resisted.
hint.failureConsequences: What happens when casting goes wrong.
hint.recoveryOrRecharge: How soon it can be cast again.
hint.resistanceOrSavingThrow: How a target can resist it.
hint.usageLimits: How often it can be used.
hint.associatedDeitiesOrPatrons: The gods or patrons who grant or favor it.
hint.prerequisiteMagic: Magic that must be mastered first.
hint.publicPerception: How ordinary people see it — and those who cast it.
hint.regulatingOrganizations: Organizations that control or police it.
hint.associatedLaws: Laws this document creates, records or disputes.
hint.keyClaims: The most important things it asserts — true or not.
hint.language: The language it's written in. Can the party even read it?
hint.subjects: Anything the document is about: people, places, events, other documents.
hint.summaryOfContents: What it says, in a sentence or two.
hint.accessLevel: Who is allowed to read it — and how hard it is to get.
hint.authenticity: Is it genuine? A forgery can be as powerful as the real thing.
hint.documentType: What kind of document this is.
hint.physicalCondition: What shape it's in. Missing pages hide the best secrets.
hint.originalDocument: The original, if this is a copy or translation.
hint.endonym: What its speakers call the language in the language itself.
hint.languageFamily: The family of related languages it belongs to.
hint.originType: How it came to be: grown over centuries, invented, given by gods?
hint.varietyType: Whether this is a full language or a variety of one.
hint.derivedLanguages: Languages that grew out of this one.
hint.dialects: Regional or social varieties of it.
hint.influencedBy: Languages it borrowed words or grammar from.
hint.mutuallyIntelligibleLanguages: Languages whose speakers can more or less understand each other.
hint.communicationModes: How it's communicated. Pick every mode that applies.
hint.officialRecognition: Territories or organizations that make it official.
hint.alphabetOrSymbols: What its writing looks like: letters, runes, glyphs, knots?
hint.scriptNames: The names of the scripts used to write it.
hint.associatedMagic: Magic tied to the language: spells, faiths, enchanted items.
hint.restrictionsOnUse: Laws that limit or forbid speaking it.
hint.tabooWords: Words never to be spoken, and what happens if they are.
